reason: The electrolyzer stack and gas-control manifold are natural components of the installation.
expectation: The manifold should connect to the stack to control its gas outputs.

effect: The stack and manifold form a rack with separate gas outlets; its water feed still needs the processor’s polishing outlet.
reaction: The separate outlet paths make the installation’s purpose clearer.
reason: The rack explicitly needs polished water from the processor.
expectation: The rack will connect to the polished-water feed.

effect: The electrolyzer now has polished water, power and cooling; the remaining goal is to collect its gases separately.
reaction: The separate circuits make the next connection clear.
reason: The gas cylinders are the available containers for the electrolyzer's separate outputs.
expectation: The cylinders will connect to the separate gas circuits.

effect: The cylinders complete the separate hydrogen and oxygen circuits, and the chapter's goals are complete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the cylinders was most worthwhile: it showed how electrolysis produces and separately conditions the gases for collection.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the water feed was fairly predictable, though its mention of power and cooling added useful context.

surprise.text: The automatic run stops when either buffer is full, a practical safeguard I had not anticipated.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each connected a component to an explicitly stated need.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the gases are used for the return journey; the practical details made this brief construction sequence engaging.
